rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords may not ask about or use criminal history or criminal background checks in rental advertising, applications, tenant selection or decision-making. This includes refusing to rent, terminating a tenancy, requiring disclosure or authorization, demanding a higher deposit or rent, refusing to add an immediate family member, or disqualifying tenants from rental assistance based on criminal history. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond. Landlords must post the Notice to Rental Applicants and Tenants on application materials, websites and frequently visited locations.
rules.key_value: Ban on criminal history inquiries and use in tenant screening
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing in Berkeley, excluding owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties where an owner of record lives in one unit as a primary residence.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; limited exemptions for public housing/Section 8 properties; owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units where an owner of record lives in one unit as a primary residence; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add or replace roommates.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages, including actual damages or three times one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; and injunctive relief.
